q: Which Philippine document cited in this module contains accessible elevator dimensions and transport-facility escalator provisions?
ref: DPWH, Amended IRR of BP 344, Accessibility Law, Appendix A (accessible elevators and transport-facility escalators).
n: The amended BP 344 IRR contains accessibility requirements including provisions for accessible elevators and escalators in transport facilities.

q: According to the Philippine Green Building Code guidance, elevator standby operation is intended primarily to:
o: Reduce energy demand during off-peak periods
ref: DPWH, Philippine Green Building Code User Guide (energy-efficiency provisions for mechanical systems, elevators, escalators/moving walks).
n: Standby modes reduce energy use when traffic is low.

q: Which combination best matches the PGB Code guidance discussed in this module?
o: VVVF drive for non-hydraulic elevators plus demand-responsive controls for escalators/moving walks
Steam elevators plus continuously running escalators
Manual elevators plus fixed-speed walks only
ref: DPWH, Philippine Green Building Code User Guide (energy-efficiency provisions for mechanical systems, elevators, escalators/moving walks).
n: The guide discusses VVVF drives for non-hydraulic elevators and sensing/control strategies that can slow or stop escalators and moving walks during no-traffic periods.

q: According to the cited amended BP 344 transport-facility provision, an escalator should have:
o: An alternative pedestrian route nearby and clearly indicated
Only a freight elevator as the alternative
No alternate route under any circumstances
ref: DPWH, Amended IRR of BP 344, Accessibility Law, Appendix A (accessible elevators and transport-facility escalators).
n: The amended BP 344 Appendix A provision for transport infrastructure states that an alternative pedestrian route must be provided near the escalator and clearly shown by signage.

q: Which approach generally reduces ventilation fan energy when full airflow is not continuously required?
o: Operating every fan at full speed at all times
Demand-based or variable-speed control where appropriate
ref: DPWH, Philippine Green Building Code User Guide (energy-efficiency provisions for mechanical systems, elevators, escalators/moving walks).
n: Controls and variable-speed operation can reduce fan energy during periods of lower demand when allowed by ventilation requirements.

q: Which escalator feature is encouraged by the Philippine Green Building Code guidance?
o: Permanent full-speed operation regardless of demand
Controls that reduce speed or stop the unit when no traffic is detected
ref: DPWH, Philippine Green Building Code User Guide (energy-efficiency provisions for mechanical systems, elevators, escalators/moving walks).
n: The PGB Code user guide calls for automatic controls using sensing/control systems so escalators and moving walks can reduce speed or stop during no-traffic periods.

q: Which elevator feature aligns with the Philippine Green Building Code guidance?
o: Keeping all car lights on permanently even when idle
Automatic car-lighting switch-off after a period of inactive use
Operating at maximum speed while empty
ref: DPWH, Philippine Green Building Code User Guide (energy-efficiency provisions for mechanical systems, elevators, escalators/moving walks).
n: The guide includes efficient car/display lighting, automatic switch-off after inactivity, and standby operation during off-peak periods.

q: The Philippine Green Building Code guidance recommends moving walks with:
o: Automatic controls that can regulate speed or stop when no traffic is detected
ref: DPWH, Philippine Green Building Code User Guide (energy-efficiency provisions for mechanical systems, elevators, escalators/moving walks).
n: The guidance groups moving ramps/walkways with escalators and calls for sensing and control systems that can reduce speed or stop during no-traffic periods.

q: Under the same amended BP 344 provision, the accessible elevator car minimum dimensions are:
ref: DPWH, Amended IRR of BP 344, Accessibility Law, Appendix A (accessible elevators and transport-facility escalators).
n: The cited amended BP 344 provision gives a minimum car depth of 1,400 mm and width of 1,500 mm.

q: Which Philippine document in this module specifically provides energy-efficiency guidance for elevators and escalators/moving walks?
o: Philippine Green Building Code User Guide
ref: DPWH, Philippine Green Building Code User Guide (energy-efficiency provisions for mechanical systems, elevators, escalators/moving walks).
n: The DPWH Philippine Green Building Code User Guide contains provisions/guidance on energy-efficient elevators and escalators/moving ramps/walkways.

q: For an accessible route, which vertical transportation element can provide independent access between floors where stairs cannot?
ref: DPWH, Amended IRR of BP 344, Accessibility Law, Appendix A (accessible elevators and transport-facility escalators).
n: An accessible elevator can provide an accessible vertical route between levels when properly designed and located.

q: Which source establishes that utilities systems form part of the Philippine Architecture Licensure Examination coverage?
ref: PRC Board of Architecture, Architecture Licensure Examination Syllabi — Utilities Systems coverage.
n: The PRC Board of Architecture syllabus explicitly includes Utilities Systems among the licensure examination areas.

q: Which car-lighting strategy is consistent with the PGB Code guidance?
o: Efficient lighting and automatic switch-off after inactivity
Incandescent lighting kept on continuously by rule
ref: DPWH, Philippine Green Building Code User Guide (energy-efficiency provisions for mechanical systems, elevators, escalators/moving walks).
n: The guidance promotes efficient car/display lighting and automatic shutdown after a specified inactive period.

q: An architect provides only an escalator between two public levels in a facility that requires an accessible vertical route. What is the main issue?
o: The escalator must be replaced by a louver
An escalator alone generally does not provide the required accessible route
ref: DPWH, Amended IRR of BP 344, Accessibility Law, Appendix A (accessible elevators and transport-facility escalators).
n: Accessible circulation must be provided by a compliant means such as an accessible elevator or ramp where required; escalators alone are not sufficient.

q: When multiple adjoining escalators are installed in the cited BP 344 transport-facility context, at least:
o: Three upward escalators only are required
One upward and one downward escalator should be installed
ref: DPWH, Amended IRR of BP 344, Accessibility Law, Appendix A (accessible elevators and transport-facility escalators).
n: The cited amendment states that where multiple adjoining escalators are installed, at least one upward and one downward escalator shall be provided.

q: Which drive technology is specifically cited in the Philippine Green Building Code guidance for non-hydraulic elevators?
ref: DPWH, Philippine Green Building Code User Guide (energy-efficiency provisions for mechanical systems, elevators, escalators/moving walks).
n: The PGB Code user guide identifies alternating-current variable-voltage variable-frequency (VVVF) drives for non-hydraulic elevators as an energy-efficiency measure.

q: Why is soft-start technology useful in an escalator control strategy?
o: It allows controlled acceleration and can be part of an energy-efficient automatic-control system
It makes the steps disappear at the landing
ref: DPWH, Philippine Green Building Code User Guide (energy-efficiency provisions for mechanical systems, elevators, escalators/moving walks).
n: Soft-start/control technology can reduce abrupt starting loads and forms part of efficient operating strategies described in the PGB Code guidance.

q: Under the amended BP 344 provisions cited for accessible elevators, what minimum clear door opening width is specified?
ref: DPWH, Amended IRR of BP 344, Accessibility Law, Appendix A (accessible elevators and transport-facility escalators).
n: The amended BP 344 Appendix A provision states a clear elevator door opening width of at least 900 mm for the cited accessible elevator requirement.

q: The purpose of no-traffic detection on moving walks is primarily to:
o: Reduce unnecessary energy use during idle periods
Keep the unit at maximum power continuously
ref: DPWH, Philippine Green Building Code User Guide (energy-efficiency provisions for mechanical systems, elevators, escalators/moving walks).
n: Demand-responsive control reduces energy consumption when no passengers are present.

q: Why is clear elevator door width important in accessible design?
o: It must permit passage and maneuvering by wheelchair users and other mobility-device users
ref: DPWH, Amended IRR of BP 344, Accessibility Law, Appendix A (accessible elevators and transport-facility escalators).
n: Accessible entrances require sufficient clear width for mobility-device passage; the amended BP 344 provision cited specifies at least 900 mm in the relevant context.
